acceptance_criteria: Heal persistence stores only a versioned, bounded, closed evidence projection rather than raw request, crash, log, or provider payloads.
No heal, pending-heal, or control-message row contains raw chat identity, stderr, recent logs, free-form diagnosis, provider output, secret, path, token, or other sensitive forensic material.
Runtime dispatch, completion, and operator notifications carry bounded reason and diagnosis codes plus opaque private-artifact references, never raw forensic context.
POST /heal and control traffic validate strict closed schemas, reject unknown fields, enforce per-field bounds, and validate before durable projection.
Fallback messages, human reports, logs, admin notifications, and control-message ingestion use the same minimized evidence projection.
Canonical retention covers terminal and pending heal reports, control messages, and private forensic artifacts with explicit windows and protected unresolved states.
Migration irreversibly redacts, tombstones, or safely expires legacy raw-context rows without copying sensitive values into replacement public evidence.
Reserved synthetic canaries prove raw identity, stderr, recent logs, diagnosis, provider output, paths, tokens, and secrets are absent from durable rows and retransmitted payloads.
blast_radius: Every crash and operator-triggered heal entering POST /heal or the heal protocol; heal_reports, pending_heal_reports, and control_messages persistence; runtime dispatch; operator notifications; fallback and human reports; local backups and retention; and downstream agents receiving repair evidence.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if every durable and retransmitted heal representation used one strict, bounded, non-sensitive projection and all associated stores participated in evidence-aware retention. Exact-main source proves the opposite. Product policy must still approve the closed reason-code vocabulary, authorized private-artifact boundary, retention windows, unresolved-state exemptions, and legacy-row disposition coordinated with issue #2561.
impact: A crash, operator request, or provider failure can persist and retransmit raw stderr, recent logs, chat identity, free-form diagnosis, paths, tokens, secrets, and other forensic context across database rows, control messages, runtime dispatch, and operator notifications. Those stores are outside canonical retention, extending exposure through backups and routine operations.

recommended_title: security(heal): replace raw forensic context with a bounded private evidence projection
suggested_remediation: Define one versioned, strict, closed heal-evidence projection shared by HTTP ingestion, protocol validation, persistence, runtime dispatch, control messages, fallbacks, human reports, and operator notifications. Permit only bounded low-cardinality reason and diagnosis codes plus an opaque reference to a separately authorized private artifact; validate before persistence, eliminate object spreading and free-form retransmission, add transactional retention, and irreversibly redact or expire legacy raw context.
title: security(heal): raw forensic context is persisted and retransmitted as repair evidence
